slots.heading: Before You Start
slots.content: This assignment doesn't start from a blank page. It starts from Assignment 1 — your research summary, your insight list, and your Pinterest mood board. Every brief you write here has to trace back to something you already found or decided in that assignment. If a choice in this assignment can't be justified by a specific research finding, a specific insight, or a specific pin on your board, it's a guess dressed up as a decision — and it should be reworked until it isn't. The point of this assignment: in the real world, nobody designs directly from a mood board. Someone writes a brief first — a document precise enough that a photographer, a designer, or an AI tool could pick it up and actually produce the right thing without you standing over their shoulder. You're going to write three of those.

slots.heading: What You're Producing: Three Distinct Briefs
slots.content: Not one long document — three separate, focused briefs, each doing a different job:
items: Brand Idea & Philosophy Brief — what this brand believes and stands for
Product & Packaging Brief — what the actual product is and how it presents itself
Ad/Campaign Creative Brief — how this brand shows up in a campaign, and what it takes to actually produce that
slots.note: Think of them as three documents you could hand to three different people — a strategist, a packaging designer, and a director — and each would know exactly what to do.

subsections.heading: Core Idea (1–2 sentences)
subsections.content: What is this brand, in one breath? Not a tagline — the underlying idea.

subsections.heading: Philosophy / Point of View
subsections.content: Why does this brand exist? What does it believe that others in the category don't say out loud? This should connect directly to a gap or opportunity from your Assignment 1 research (e.g., \"every brand in this category talks about performance — we're the only one that talks about ritual\")."

subsections.heading: Positioning Statement
subsections.content: For [target audience], [brand] is the [category] that [key differentiator], because [reason to believe]. Pull the audience and differentiator directly from your research — don't invent a new audience here.

subsections.heading: Personality & Tone of Voice
subsections.content: 3–5 personality adjectives, and one example line of how the brand would actually talk (a tagline, a social caption, a packaging line).

subsections.heading: Name Rationale
subsections.content: If you're naming the brand, explain the reasoning in 2–3 sentences — what it signals, why it fits.

subsections.heading: Logo Direction (not the logo itself — a brief for it)
subsections.content: What does the logo need to communicate? Reference 2–3 visual styles from your mood board that it should draw from, and explicitly state what it should avoid (e.g., \"avoid the clinical, all-lowercase sans-serif look most competitors use\").

subsections.heading: Product Definition
subsections.content: What exactly is the product — format, variants, size options, price positioning (mass/premium/luxury) relative to the competitors you researched.

subsections.heading: Packaging Direction
items: Materials and structure (what it's made of, shape, how it opens/closes/is held)
Color and finish, tied to a specific insight or pin from your mood board
The one shelf-standout element — what makes this recognizable from three feet away in a crowded shelf/feed

subsections.heading: Functional-to-Emotional Bridge
subsections.content: One paragraph connecting a functional packaging choice to the emotional positioning from Brief 1 (e.g., \"the matte, screw-top cap signals ritual and control, reinforcing the 'daily ritual, not a quick fix' philosophy\").

subsections.heading: Shelf/Competitive Differentiation
subsections.content: Placed next to your 3–5 researched competitors, what makes this package unmistakably different — not just \"better,\" but different in a specific, describable way.

slots.heading: Brief 3 — Ad / Campaign Creative Brief
slots.content: This is the one that will actually get produced — treat it like a real production document.

subsections.heading: Campaign Concept (The Big Idea)
subsections.content: One or two sentences. What's the idea the whole campaign hangs on?

subsections.heading: Hero Shot Direction
subsections.content: Describe the single image that best represents this campaign — composition, what's in frame, what's the focal point, what mood it needs to hit. Be specific enough that someone else could shoot or generate it from your description alone.

subsections.heading: Stage / Environment
subsections.content: Where does this campaign live, visually? A studio setup, a real location, an abstract/surreal environment? Describe lighting, backdrop, and setting in enough detail to brief a location scout or an AI generation prompt.

subsections.heading: Models / Casting Direction
subsections.content: Who's in this campaign? Age range, look, styling, energy — tied explicitly back to the target audience you researched in Assignment 1. If the campaign deliberately avoids people (product-only, abstract), state that as a choice and explain why.

subsections.heading: Plan of Action — Creative Direction Sequence
subsections.content: List the actual assets this campaign needs, in order of priority:
subsections.note: For each, note which mood-board reference(s) it's pulling from.

subsections.heading: Production Requirements
subsections.content: What does it actually take to make this real? Cover both paths and pick the one you're proposing:
items: Traditional production: locations, photographer/videographer, stylist, models, props, post-production

AI-generated production: which tools you'd use at each stage (reference the standardized image/video workflow from earlier in the course) and where a human would still need to intervene for quality or brand consistency

slots.heading: Coherence Check (Do This Before Submitting)
slots.content: For each of the three briefs, answer in one line: which specific research finding, insight, or mood-board pin does this trace back to? If you can't answer that for a major decision in any brief, go back and fix it — this is the check that keeps the whole assignment from becoming three disconnected documents.

slots.heading: Deliverable & Submission
slots.content: Submit all three briefs as one package, clearly labeled, plus the one-line coherence answers above each brief.

rows: Every major decision across all three briefs connects to something specific from Assignment 1
Briefs are precise enough that someone else could execute from them without guessing
The brand philosophy, the packaging, and the campaign all feel like they belong to the same brand
The production requirements are genuinely achievable, or a genuinely thought-through AI-generation path
The direction has a specific point of view — it doesn't read like a generic version of the category leader
